description: A reading collection of language-model distillation methods, analyses, applications, and related foundations.

papers.title: A Reduction of Imitation Learning and Structured Prediction to No-Regret Online Learning
papers.description: DAgger collects states visited by the learner or an optional learner–expert mixture, obtains expert action labels, and retrains on the accumulated data. Its no-regret analysis concerns sequential imitation under additional assumptions, not language-model token distillation.
papers.objective: Minimize a supervised surrogate loss against expert actions on aggregated visited states.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Nov 2010 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Mar 2011 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
papers.description: Classical distillation trains a smaller model to match a pretrained model’s softened class probabilities on a fixed transfer set, optionally adding a loss on known labels. Its experiments concern classification and speech acoustic models, not student-generated language prefixes.
papers.objective: Cross-entropy against high-temperature soft targets, optionally combined with cross-entropy against correct labels.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 9 Mar 2015]

papers.title: Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation
papers.description: For neural machine translation, sequence-level distillation trains a student on teacher beam-search outputs; an alternative selects a beam candidate close to the reference translation. These are teacher-generated training targets, not trajectories sampled from the student during learning.
papers.objective: Student negative log-likelihood of a selected teacher beam-search sequence, either the highest-scoring output or a candidate selected for similarity to the reference.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Jun 2016 ( v1 ), last revised 22 Sep 2016 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
papers.description: This study estimates how to allocate a fixed pre-training compute budget between language-model size and training tokens by fitting losses from varied training runs. Its proposed allocation concerns autoregressive pre-training, not the additional generation, teacher, and update costs of on-policy distillation.
papers.objective: Minimize estimated final language-model pre-training loss under a fixed compute budget by choosing model size and training-token count.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Mar 2022]

papers.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
papers.description: This evaluation framework organizes language-model use cases and metrics, then benchmarks models across shared scenarios using multiple measures beyond accuracy. Its implemented coverage is selective, and its standardized prompting evaluations are not a training or on-policy distillation method.
papers.objective: Evaluate prompted language models on shared scenarios using accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, and efficiency measures where applicable.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 16 Nov 2022 ( v1 ), last revised 1 Oct 2023 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes
papers.description: A teacher generates labels and natural-language rationales for task examples; a smaller model learns separate label-prediction and rationale-generation tasks from those outputs. Training uses collected teacher responses rather than student-visited prefixes, and the student can predict labels without requesting a rationale at test time.
papers.objective: Minimize a weighted sum of token cross-entropy losses for predicting task labels and generating teacher-provided rationales.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 May 2023 ( v1 ), last revised 5 Jul 2023 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: The False Promise of Imitating Proprietary LLMs
papers.description: This study fine-tunes models on previously collected outputs from a proprietary language model and compares human ratings with targeted task evaluations. The imitators reproduce response style and instruction following, but show limited gains on tasks poorly represented in the imitation data.
papers.objective: Supervised language-model loss on collected teacher outputs, applied only to model-output tokens.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 May 2023]

papers.title: MiniLLM: On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models
papers.description: MiniLLM targets sequence-level reverse KL using student-generated responses and teacher probabilities. Its update separates an immediate full-vocabulary term from estimated future effects, with teacher-mixed sampling and other stabilizers; its reported evaluation centers on instruction following, not a general rule favoring reverse KL.
papers.objective: Minimize sequence-level student-to-teacher reverse KL using a decomposed gradient with an immediate conditional term and a future-return policy-gradient term; training also includes a pretraining language-model loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 Jun 2023 ( v1 ), last revised 31 Jan 2026 (this version, v6)]

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models: Learning from Self-Generated Mistakes
papers.description: GKD queries teacher next-token distributions on prefixes from student-generated sequences, optionally mixing them with fixed examples, and minimizes a chosen conditional divergence without backpropagating through sampling. Only the student-generated portion of that mixture is on-policy.
papers.objective: Minimize a chosen teacher–student next-token divergence on sampled or fixed prefixes: forward KL, reverse KL, or generalized Jensen–Shannon divergence. Do not backpropagate through student sampling.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 23 Jun 2023 ( v1 ), last revised 17 Jan 2024 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: f-Divergence Minimization for Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation
papers.description: f-DISTILL develops step-wise training losses for several sequence-level divergence objectives. Some variants sample current students while symmetric-loss variants also use fixed teacher samples; the student-sampling path is stop-gradient, and the implemented Jensen–Shannon conditional is an approximation rather than the exact sequence divergence.
papers.objective: Minimize step-wise conditional losses for forward KL, reverse KL, approximate Jensen–Shannon divergence, or an upper bound on total variation; sampled student prefixes receive no gradient through their sampling distribution.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 Jul 2023]

papers.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
papers.description: PagedAttention stores attention key–value caches in fixed-size blocks that need not occupy contiguous memory, allowing an LLM serving engine to allocate and share cache space across sequences. It addresses generation-time memory management, not teacher supervision or a distillation update.
papers.objective: N/A
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Sep 2023]

papers.title: DistillSpec: Improving Speculative Decoding via Knowledge Distillation
papers.description: DistillSpec trains a speculative-decoding draft model on draft-generated contexts to match a target model’s next-token distributions, choosing the divergence according to the task and decoding strategy. Its purpose is draft–target alignment for deployment-time verification, not faster distillation training.
papers.objective: Minimize a chosen divergence between target and draft next-token distributions along training sequences; the studied choices include forward KL, reverse KL, Jensen–Shannon divergence, and total variation distance.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Oct 2023 ( v1 ), last revised 31 Mar 2024 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models
papers.description: SPIN repeatedly generates responses from a previous version of a supervised fine-tuned model and trains the next version to favor existing human demonstrations over those responses. Its comparison target is a fixed demonstration dataset, not a teacher’s token distributions on current student rollouts.
papers.objective: Minimize a logistic loss that favors human responses over previous-model responses using their relative sequence log probabilities against the previous model.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Jan 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 14 Jun 2024 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: DistiLLM: Towards Streamlined Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.description: DistiLLM combines skewed token-distribution matching with an adaptive schedule that draws from fixed data or a replay buffer of student-generated responses. Because buffered responses are reused after collection, its data strategy is partly off-policy rather than continuously fresh student rollout.
papers.objective: Minimize token-level skewed forward or reverse KL between teacher and student distributions on fixed or replayed student-generated sequences; the reported setup uses skewed reverse KL.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 6 Feb 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Jul 2024 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation for Autoregressive Language Models
papers.description: This paper separates token-level teacher matching into target-token and non-target-token terms, then adapts their use according to teacher uncertainty: easy tokens omit target-oriented teaching, while hard tokens retain both terms. Its described training uses an instruction-response dataset, not a required student-rollout procedure.
papers.objective: Teacher–student target-versus-nontarget matching for hard tokens; non-target distribution matching without the target-oriented term for easy tokens.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 19 Feb 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 17 Jun 2024 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: PromptKD: Distilling Student-Friendly Knowledge for Generative Language Models via Prompt Tuning
papers.description: On student-generated responses, PromptKD alternates student-guided tuning of soft teacher prompts with reverse-KL updates of the student toward the prompted teacher. Teacher weights stay fixed, while an early, decaying regularizer limits how far the prompted teacher departs from its unprompted distribution.
papers.objective: Update prompts using teacher-to-student KL plus a decaying prompted-to-unprompted-teacher KL regularizer; update the student using student-to-prompted-teacher reverse KL on student-generated response prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 Feb 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 27 Sep 2024 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: A Survey on Knowledge Distillation of Large Language Models
papers.description: This survey organizes language-model knowledge distillation by algorithms, transferred skills, and domain-specific uses, including data augmentation and self-generated knowledge. It synthesizes prior work rather than introducing a training rule or establishing which surveyed methods use student-generated prefixes.
papers.objective: N/A
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 Feb 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 21 Oct 2024 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: Rethinking Kullback-Leibler Divergence in Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.description: AKL weights forward and reverse token KL according to teacher–student gaps in the distribution’s head and tail, motivated by their different early training behavior. The study uses instruction-response training data and does not establish distillation on student-generated prefixes.
papers.objective: An adaptive weighted sum of teacher-to-student forward KL and student-to-teacher reverse KL, with weights set by head- and tail-distribution gaps.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Apr 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 8 Dec 2024 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: Gemma 2: Improving Open Language Models at a Practical Size
papers.description: Gemma 2 pretrains its smaller models by matching a larger teacher’s next-token probabilities on training text. The report separately describes post-training distillation on the student’s distribution, but does not specify the loss or sampling procedure for that stage.
papers.objective: Pretraining minimizes teacher-probability-weighted negative log-likelihood of student next-token predictions; the post-training distillation loss is not specified.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 31 Jul 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 2 Oct 2024 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework
papers.description: HybridFlow is an RLHF execution framework that centrally coordinates dependencies between distributed models while letting each model manage its own computation. It also reshards actor weights between generation and training; these systems mechanisms do not specify teacher targets for on-policy distillation.
papers.objective: N/A
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Sep 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 2 Oct 2024 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Speculative Knowledge Distillation: Bridging the Teacher-Student Gap Through Interleaved Sampling
papers.description: Speculative Knowledge Distillation builds training sequences by accepting student-proposed tokens that rank highly under the teacher and replacing rejected tokens with teacher samples. It then matches teacher and student token distributions on those mixed trajectories, rather than training solely on unmodified student rollouts.
papers.objective: Minimize token-level divergence between teacher and student distributions on interleaved teacher–student sequences.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 Oct 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 27 Apr 2025 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: MiniPLM: Knowledge Distillation for Pre-Training Language Models
papers.description: MiniPLM selects pre-training texts offline using the probability difference between a teacher and a small reference model, then trains students with ordinary next-token prediction on the selected corpus. Selection does not use current student rollouts or require teacher inference during student training.
papers.objective: Offline teacher–reference likelihood-difference selection, followed by student next-token cross-entropy on the selected corpus.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 22 Oct 2024 ( v1 ), last revised 19 Mar 2025 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
papers.description: DeepSeek-R1 develops reasoning through reinforcement learning and a staged supervised training pipeline. Its smaller distilled models learn from curated model-generated responses using supervised fine-tuning only; this distillation stage does not train on the smaller students’ own rollouts.
papers.objective: The main models use GRPO and staged supervised/reinforcement learning; smaller-model distillation uses supervised fine-tuning on curated model-generated responses, without a reinforcement learning stage.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 22 Jan 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 4 Jan 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: On Teacher Hacking in Language Model Distillation
papers.description: The teacher-hacking study separates progress toward a distillation teacher from progress toward an independently evaluated oracle. Controlled comparisons show that refreshing teacher or student generations can reduce the divergence between these metrics, with task-dependent effects from prompt diversity.
papers.objective: Track teacher-proxy and oracle metrics across data-refresh regimes
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 4 Feb 2025]

papers.title: Distillation Scaling Laws
papers.description: This study fits a scaling law for student validation cross-entropy as teacher quality, student size and distillation data vary, then examines compute allocation with different teacher-cost assumptions. It analyzes distillation pre-training, not an on-policy rollout or refresh procedure.
papers.objective: Analyze student validation cross-entropy under data after teacher-target next-token cross-entropy distillation; compare compute allocations that include or amortize teacher costs.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Feb 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 25 Jul 2025 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: AlignDistil: Token-Level Language Model Alignment as Adaptive Policy Distillation
papers.description: AlignDistil constructs a token-level target by extrapolating logits from normal and reverse preference-trained models, with token-specific weights based on their distributional difference. It matches this target on student-sampled prefixes, but also provides an off-policy loss on fixed responses.
papers.objective: Minimize token-weighted KL from the student distribution to the extrapolated target distribution, on either student-sampled or fixed response prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 4 Mar 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 23 Jul 2025 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: DistiLLM-2: A Contrastive Approach Boosts the Distillation of LLMs
papers.description: DistiLLM-2 applies skewed forward divergence to teacher-generated responses and skewed reverse divergence to student-generated responses. The paper proposes adaptive skew and loss weighting; student responses are generated before each epoch and reused within it.
papers.objective: A weighted sum of skewed forward KL on teacher responses and skewed reverse KL on student responses. Adaptive skew and changing loss weights are proposed components of the paper’s recipe.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Mar 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 30 May 2025 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: A Dual-Space Framework for General Knowledge Distillation of Large Language Models
papers.description: DSKD constructs comparable teacher and student output spaces through learned projections. Cross-tokenizer losses use exactly aligned positions; the student-space term also masks positions where the projected teacher fails to reproduce its top prediction. The method does not provide a lossless mapping between arbitrary tokenizers.
papers.objective: Minimize distribution-matching losses in both output spaces plus cross-entropy for the teacher-to-student projector to predict the teacher’s top token; the distribution divergence is selectable.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 Apr 2025]

papers.title: Qwen3 Technical Report
papers.description: The report describes a small-model compression pipeline that uses off-policy transfer from stronger models before on-policy distillation with teacher-logit guidance. It also describes separate supervised and reinforcement-learning stages for preparing larger models; its student-stage comparison does not account for preparing the stronger teacher.
papers.objective: Off-policy knowledge transfer followed by on-policy teacher-logit distillation for smaller models.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 May 2025]

papers.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Works in Generative Models: A Minimal Working Explanation
papers.description: This analysis asks how teacher selectivity changes a distilled generator’s balance between sample quality and distributional coverage. Gaussian-mixture simulations and language-model pretraining experiments find higher precision with lower recall when teacher samples become more selective; they do not test on-policy distillation or post-training.
papers.objective: Analyze the precision–recall effect of forward-KL teacher-to-student matching; the language-model students are trained by next-token prediction on temperature-controlled teacher samples.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 19 May 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 14 Jan 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Online Knowledge Distillation with Reward Guidance
papers.description: White-box MM-PbKD matches teacher-weighted Q moments at student-visited states under preference-derived constraints. Comparisons with fixed-preference training and a separate RLHF-plus-KD pipeline support this joint formulation without establishing full teacher-policy recovery.
papers.objective: Preference-constrained minimax Q-moment matching
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 May 2025]

papers.title: KDRL: Post-Training Reasoning LLMs via Unified Knowledge Distillation and Reinforcement Learning
papers.description: KDRL combines rule-based outcome optimization on student reasoning rollouts with a directly backpropagated sampled-token squared-log-ratio loss toward the teacher. It also tests omitting this auxiliary loss for rewarded responses; the k2 surrogate is distinct from an exact full-vocabulary reverse-KL gradient.
papers.objective: Maximize group-relative, rule-based outcome reward while minimizing an auxiliary k2 approximation to reverse KL from student to teacher on student rollouts; optionally omit distillation loss for rewarded responses.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Jun 2025]

papers.title: Distillation of Large Language Models via Concrete Score Matching
papers.description: Concrete Score Distillation matches weighted teacher–student logit differences across vocabulary pairs, allowing additive logit shifts. Factorized weights make gradient computation linear in vocabulary size. The objective requires a shared vocabulary and can complement on-policy training without itself requiring student rollouts.
papers.objective: Weighted squared error between teacher and student pairwise next-token logit differences, using detached factorized weights; weights may depend on teacher or student probabilities.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 30 Sep 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 30 May 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: AdaSwitch: Balancing Exploration and Guidance in Knowledge Distillation via Adaptive Switching
papers.description: AdaSwitch starts each training rollout with student-generated tokens, then lets the teacher finish when next-token divergence exceeds a threshold based on recent divergences. The student matches teacher token distributions along the mixed sequence; its one-time handoff leaves the remainder teacher-generated rather than returning control to the student.
papers.objective: Mean teacher-to-student next-token distribution divergence over the mixed generated sequence, with forward KL given as an instantiation.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 9 Oct 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 19 Mar 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Student-generated trajectories are scored using teacher log probabilities for sampled tokens, and a policy-gradient-style update uses the negative log-ratio as per-token feedback. This implementation uses immediate next-token credit, not full-vocabulary teacher distributions or future-token returns; the citation here supports sampled-token supervision.
papers.objective: Minimize immediate per-token reverse KL on student-sampled prefixes, using sampled student-minus-teacher token log probabilities as negative advantages in an importance-sampling policy-gradient update.

papers.title: VOLD: Reasoning Transfer from LLMs to Vision-Language Models via On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: VOLD transfers text reasoning into a vision-language model through teacher-trace preparation followed by joint reward learning and student-prefix distillation. Controlled comparisons show that the value of the distillation stage depends on preparation and selective supervision, while inconsistent divergence descriptions limit a precise estimator interpretation.
papers.objective: Teacher-trace preparation followed by selective distillation and RL
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 Oct 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Jun 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: SelecTKD: Selective Token-Weighted Knowledge Distillation for LLMs
papers.description: SelecTKD weights teacher–student token divergences using teacher verification of student proposals. Experiments adding the selector to GKD and mixed-source distillation establish an OPD component, while the separate offline geometry study does not determine the provenance of every training prefix.
papers.objective: Verification-weighted conditional teacher–student divergence
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Oct 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Nov 2025 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Black-Box On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models
papers.description: GAD trains a discriminator to score teacher responses above current student responses, then uses its scalar score as reinforcement-learning feedback for student rollouts. This permits black-box teacher access, but the feedback is a learned response-level proxy, not teacher token probabilities.
papers.objective: A Bradley–Terry pairwise loss trains the discriminator to prefer teacher responses; policy-gradient training maximizes its scalar score for student-generated responses, following a teacher-response likelihood warmup.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 Nov 2025 ( v1 ), last revised 8 Jan 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: A Note on Hybrid Online Reinforcement and Imitation Learning for LLMs: Formulations and Algorithms
papers.description: This note combines trajectory-level student-to-reference KL with task reward, separating an analytic local token-KL gradient from a sampled gradient for future divergence and rewards. It supplies a gradient decomposition and proposed algorithm, while leaving empirical training validation to future work.
papers.objective: Minimize trajectory-level student-to-reference KL minus expected task reward; compute the local token-KL gradient analytically and estimate future divergence and reward effects by policy gradient.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Dec 2025]

papers.title: MiMo-V2-Flash Technical Report
papers.description: The report uses multi-teacher on-policy distillation to consolidate domain-specialist capabilities, combining dense token-level teacher rewards with verifiable outcome rewards. This is one stage of a broader post-training pipeline, so the final model’s capabilities cannot be attributed to distillation alone.
papers.objective: Dense token-level rewards from specialized teachers combined with verifiable outcome-based rewards.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 6 Jan 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 8 Jan 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Stable On-Policy Distillation through Adaptive Target Reformulation
papers.description: Veto forms a product target from teacher probabilities and a detached student contribution. Its fixed-coefficient comparison tests target reweighting independently of annealing; the paper's parameter-gradient stability guarantee is not established by that empirical result.
papers.objective: Forward KL to a detached teacher–student product target; fixed-coefficient experiments compare target reweighting.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Jan 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 11 Jul 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: ORBIT: On-policy Exploration-Exploitation for Controllable Multi-Budget Reasoning
papers.description: ORBIT trains reasoning-budget specialists through staged reinforcement learning under progressively tighter context limits, then initializes a unified student by merging them and distills their mode-specific behavior on student-generated responses. Its evaluation mainly covers reasoning tasks with structured correctness signals.
papers.objective: Correctness-reward reinforcement learning for budget-specific experts, followed by mode-conditioned reverse KL against the corresponding expert on student-sampled responses.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 Jan 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Apr 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Distribution-Aligned Sequence Distillation for Superior Long-CoT Reasoning
papers.description: DASD includes a mixed-policy stage in which a teacher completes retained prefixes from student-generated reasoning traces. Its masking comparison studies whether retaining the student segment helps subsequent fine-tuning, alongside substantial offline sequence-distillation stages.
papers.objective: Cross-entropy on student-prefix and teacher-continuation sequences
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 Jan 2026]

papers.title: CORD: Bridging the Audio-Text Reasoning Gap via Weighted On-policy Cross-modal Distillation
papers.description: CORD aligns audio-generated prefixes with text-conditioned predictions through divergence- and position-weighted reverse KL, alongside judge-rewarded sequence optimization. A cumulative comparison supports a small additional benefit from weighting, while the joint rollout-group configuration remains unclear.
papers.objective: Weighted cross-modal reverse KL + judge-rewarded sequence optimization
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 23 Jan 2026]

papers.title: Self-Distilled Reasoner: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.description: OPSD distills a reference-solution-conditioned teacher into a problem-only student on the student’s rollout prefixes. Its main experiments freeze the initial teacher and use full-vocabulary forward KL with pointwise clipping; the reported selected-checkpoint comparisons favor OPSD over GRPO at 1.7B, 4B, and 8B.
papers.objective: Forward KL from the solution-conditioned teacher to the student on student-generated prefixes, clipping individual vocabulary contributions and differentiating only through the student. A sampled-token policy-gradient variant is evaluated separately.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 Jan 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 20 Mar 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning
papers.description: SDFT distills a demonstration-conditioned EMA teacher on fresh student rollouts. Its practical experiments use full-vocabulary forward KL despite the paper’s reverse-KL motivation; they study continual skill and knowledge adaptation, rely on effective in-context learning, and reduce rather than eliminate forgetting.
papers.objective: Per-token forward KL from the demonstration-conditioned teacher to the student over the full vocabulary, treating teacher predictions as fixed during each update and then updating teacher parameters by EMA.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 Jan 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 7 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning via Self-Distillation
papers.description: SDPO samples current-policy attempts, then conditions that policy on feedback to re-evaluate those attempts as a self-teacher and distills its next-token distributions into the student. When only scalar outcomes are available, successful attempts can supply feedback; the mechanism relies on the model’s ability to use that context.
papers.objective: Minimize next-token KL from the student to a feedback-conditioned, stop-gradient self-teacher along student-generated attempts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Jan 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Feb 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: KEPO: Knowledge-Enhanced Preference Optimization for Multimodal Reasoning with Applications to Medical VQA
papers.description: KEPO combines reward-thresholded teacher matching with a separate recovery branch for rollout groups that receive no positive reward. Gating and recovery comparisons support these two changes, while the threshold includes format reward and should not be described as a correctness-only filter.
papers.objective: Reward-gated teacher distillation plus hinted recovery and RL
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 30 Jan 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 11 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Making Expert Reasoning Learnable with Self-Distillation
papers.description: DAIL uses an expert-solution-conditioned self-teacher to accept or replace student proposals and then trains on the collected prefixes with a negative-reference contrast. Its sampling and objective comparisons support the tested construction, with mixed generation helping long-reasoning models more consistently than shorter-reasoning variants.
papers.objective: Positive teacher KL minus negative-reference KL on collected prefixes
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Feb 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Expanding the Capabilities of Reinforcement Learning via Text Feedback
papers.description: In two-turn training, the policy revises its own answer after receiving a critique. Self-distillation uses reward-weighted revisions to train the original-prompt policy, while a separate variant predicts critiques alongside multi-turn RL. Both target first-turn performance when external feedback is unavailable at inference.
papers.objective: Self-distillation combines a first-turn-reward-baselined policy-gradient update on revised answers under the original prompt with multi-turn RL. Feedback modeling instead combines multi-turn RL with cross-entropy prediction of critique tokens.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Feb 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 11 Feb 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Privileged Information Distillation for Language Models
papers.description: The study compares privileged-information transfer through teacher-sampled π-Distill and a separate student-sampled OPSD procedure. Its experiments vary information type, model and objective strength, including failure cases. The teacher-sampled main algorithm and the on-policy comparison should be distinguished.
papers.objective: π-Distill combines teacher-sampled reward and a teacher-to-stopped-student KL penalty with importance-weighted student learning and a teacher-to-student KL penalty on those trajectories. The on-policy alternative uses student-sampled environment reward minus student-to-stopped-teacher KL.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 4 Feb 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Feb 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Multi-Token Prediction via Self-Distillation
papers.description: A pretrained autoregressive model learns to propose token blocks in one pass while a frozen copy scores the student’s own greedy proposals. The resulting predictor uses confidence-adaptive decoding; the conversion is evaluated on selected generation tasks rather than all text domains.
papers.objective: Minimize the student’s negative log probability of its own greedy token block, weighted by teacher feedback on that block; the main training runs use hard greedy teacher feedback.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 5 Feb 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 23 Apr 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Learning beyond Teacher: Generalized On-Policy Distillation with Reward Extrapolation
papers.description: Generalized on-policy distillation scores student-generated trajectories with a teacher-to-reference log-probability ratio, scales that implicit reward, and penalizes divergence from the reference. Its extrapolation variants are studied in math and code; using a teacher’s pre-RL checkpoint as the reference requires access to that checkpoint.
papers.objective: Maximize a scaled teacher-to-reference log-probability reward on student-generated responses, minus reverse KL divergence from the student to the reference.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Feb 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 26 Feb 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Towards On-Policy SFT: Distribution Discriminant Theory and its Applications in LLM Training
papers.description: Hinted Decoding constructs training traces by mixing answer-conditioned and question-only predictions from the same model at shared prefixes. Adaptive mixing and an answer-region switch improve the tested supervised-training recipe, but the traces are collected before optimization rather than refreshed throughout training.
papers.objective: Supervised learning on entropy-mixed privileged and unassisted traces
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Feb 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 14 Mar 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: $X$-KD: General Experiential Knowledge Distillation for Large Language Models
papers.description: The generalized X-KD branch adds a learned reward-modeling and temporal-consistency term to GKD on mixed student and supervised prefixes. Comparisons with GKD show setting-dependent gains, while its black-box sequence branch uses offline teacher responses and does not establish recovery of the teacher's original reward.
papers.objective: Mixed-prefix GKD plus learned temporal-consistency constraints
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 Feb 2026]

papers.title: Fast and Effective On-policy Distillation from Reasoning Prefixes
papers.description: The method stops student-generated rollouts at a training prefix and applies token-level teacher supervision only there, with a schedule that lengthens the prefix over training. It is evaluated on long reasoning outputs; behaviors that emerge late receive less direct supervision.
papers.objective: Minimize sampled reverse KL from student to teacher over tokens in the generated prefix, with an importance-sampling correction during updates.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 16 Feb 2026]

papers.title: GATES: Self-Distillation under Privileged Context with Consensus Gating
papers.description: A model samples document-conditioned tutor reasoning, uses agreement on final answers to gate training, and teaches its document-free role through eligible full trajectories. Training is primarily off-policy imitation, supplemented by student-rollout updates; consensus can still reflect shared tutor errors.
papers.objective: Combine negative log-likelihood on consensus-eligible tutor trajectories with a smaller student-rollout loss weighted by clipped tutor-minus-student token log-probabilities; skip questions lacking consensus.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 24 Feb 2026]

papers.title: Explain in Your Own Words: Improving Reasoning via Token-Selective Dual Knowledge Distillation
papers.description: TSD-KD trains on student-generated reasoning using teacher rankings of student-proposed token candidates in an early response segment, alongside distribution matching gated by the student–teacher uncertainty gap and selective entropy minimization. The ranking loss supplies preferences, not full-distribution matching.
papers.objective: A weighted sum of teacher-ranking negative log-likelihood for student token candidates, uncertainty-gap-gated generalized Jensen–Shannon divergence, and entropy minimization on selected uncertain student tokens.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Feb 2026]

papers.title: CRISP: Compressed Reasoning via Iterative Self-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This reasoning-compression method scores student-generated continuations with a self-teacher given a conciseness instruction, then minimizes token-level reverse KL with periodic teacher refreshes. The teacher receives no ground-truth solution, and excessive compression can hurt harder problems.
papers.objective: Minimize per-token reverse KL from the student to a stop-gradient, conciseness-conditioned self-teacher on student rollouts.

papers.title: Entropy-Aware On-Policy Distillation of Language Models
papers.description: Entropy-aware on-policy distillation uses student rollouts and retains a sampled, clipped reverse-KL update at every token, adding teacher-top-token forward KL where teacher entropy is high. The two terms can act together; its reported validation concentrates on mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: Combine a sampled, clipped reverse-KL policy-update surrogate with forward KL over the teacher’s renormalized top tokens when teacher entropy exceeds a threshold.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Mar 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 12 Jun 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: OpenClaw-RL: Train Any Agent Simply by Talking
papers.description: OpenClaw-RL turns subsequent interaction feedback into hints for a privileged self-teacher that scores the student’s original response prefixes. The updated report compares overlap-based hint selection with random hints and tests support and clipping choices. Its asynchronous agent results have task-specific training and evaluation limits.
papers.objective: A PPO-style clipped update combines a judged scalar reward with token-level teacher–student log-probability differences on hint-accepted turns.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Mar 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 11 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Scaling Reasoning Efficiently via Relaxed On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: REOPOLD updates on student-generated reasoning with sampled-token teacher–student log-likelihood ratios treated as stopped-gradient rewards. It floors strongly negative rewards and changes token selection from reward-based filtering to high-entropy selection; its guidance does not match full teacher distributions at every token.
papers.objective: An importance-weighted policy-gradient objective uses stopped-gradient, lower-clipped teacher–student token log-likelihood ratios, with phase-dependent token masks.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 11 Mar 2026]

papers.title: PACED: Distillation and On-Policy Self-Distillation at the Frontier of Student Competence
papers.description: PACED weights each problem’s distillation loss by a pass-rate-based measure of student competence. Its forward-KL track uses teacher-forced reference sequences, whereas its reverse-KL self-distillation track uses student rollouts; the reported single-loss experiments estimate weights once rather than continuously adapting them.
papers.objective: Pass-rate-weighted forward KL on teacher reference sequences or pass-rate-weighted reverse KL on student-generated sequences, depending on the training track.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 11 Mar 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 9 Apr 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Online Experiential Learning for Language Models
papers.description: The method extracts reusable knowledge from deployment trajectories, then trains student-generated single-turn responses from recorded interaction prefixes against a knowledge-conditioned self-teacher. Consolidation needs no access to the user-side environment; the reported experiments use text-based games.
papers.objective: Minimize token-level reverse KL from the student to a frozen, knowledge-conditioned self-teacher on student-generated responses.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 17 Mar 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Nemotron-Cascade 2: Post-Training LLMs with Cascade RL and Multi-Domain On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Nemotron-Cascade 2 selects strong intermediate checkpoints as domain teachers and distills their sampled-token guidance on student responses during cascade training. Truncated importance weights address differences between generation and training policies; the final model also reflects supervised training and multiple reinforcement learning stages.
papers.objective: A sampled-token policy-gradient surrogate uses stopped domain-teacher-minus-student log probabilities, with truncated importance weights correcting generation-policy versus training-policy mismatch; MOPD is a separate stage within the wider cascade pipeline.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 19 Mar 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 22 Mar 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Why Does Self-Distillation (Sometimes) Degrade the Reasoning Capability of LLMs?
papers.description: In the studied mathematical-reasoning settings, solution-conditioned self-distillation is associated with shorter responses, reduced uncertainty expression, and poorer OOD performance.
papers.objective: Analyzes student-to-context-conditioned-teacher next-token KL on student-generated responses, with teacher predictions stop-gradient, alongside controlled changes to teacher context and task coverage.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Mar 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 18 Aug 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: Revisiting On-Policy Distillation: Empirical Failure Modes and Simple Fixes
papers.description: This paper analyzes why sampled-token supervision can become brittle on student rollouts, then compares renormalized teacher and student distributions over the teacher’s top-ranked tokens at each prefix. The update remains token-local rather than optimizing sequence-level reverse KL.
papers.objective: Average truncated reverse KL between student and teacher distributions renormalized over the teacher’s top-ranked tokens at positions in student rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 Mar 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 27 Apr 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Unifying Group-Relative and Self-Distillation Policy Optimization via Sample Routing
papers.description: Sample routing sends correct student rollouts, and failures lacking teacher information, to reward-based policy optimization; failures with usable feedback receive distributional correction from a privileged-context self-teacher. Teacher-entropy weighting reduces uncertain token targets, so distillation does not supervise every failed rollout.
papers.objective: A clipped group-relative reward objective for one branch, and entropy-weighted token-level divergence from a stopped-gradient, feedback-conditioned self-teacher for eligible failed rollouts.

papers.title: Self-Distilled RLVR
papers.description: The RLSD study tracks references to unavailable context, validation accuracy, and teacher-student divergence during privileged-context self-distillation. Its full-distribution and restricted-target comparisons provide an empirical failure diagnostic, but do not establish inevitable leakage or a leakage-free guarantee for reward reweighting.
papers.objective: Diagnose unavailable-context references during privileged self-distillation
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 8 Apr 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Demystifying OPD: Length Inflation and Stabilization Strategies for Large Language Models
papers.description: Stable-OPD studies abrupt generation-budget exhaustion and accuracy deterioration during distillation, and compares adding reference-policy anchoring and off-policy demonstrations. Its intervention evidence is setting-specific; the printed repetition-rate condition does not consistently define the reported metric.
papers.objective: A clipped policy-gradient update using sampled-token teacher-minus-student log-likelihood advantages, combined with supervised loss on fixed demonstrations and a student-to-reference per-prefix KL penalty.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 9 Apr 2026]

papers.title: Skill-SD: Skill-Conditioned Self-Distillation for Multi-turn LLM Agents
papers.description: For multi-turn agents, Skill-SD summarizes completed trajectories into skills available to a periodically synchronized teacher. The student acts without those skills and receives token-level self-distillation alongside task-reward optimization; the evidence concerns the tested agent environments.
papers.objective: Group-relative policy optimization on trajectory completion rewards plus an importance-weighted sampled-token reverse-KL self-distillation loss against the skill-conditioned teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Apr 2026]

papers.title: SCOPE: Signal-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation Enhancement with Dual-Path Adaptive Weighting
papers.description: SCOPE includes a diagnostic that groups erroneous student responses by teacher perplexity and tests teacher recovery after prefix truncation. Lower perplexity is associated with higher recovery in its mathematical-reasoning setting. This supports a bounded diagnostic comparison, without certifying each teacher token target or the effect of the proposed weighting implementation.
papers.objective: Diagnostic association between teacher perplexity of erroneous student trajectories and recovery from truncated prefixes. Training-weight and universal reliability claims are separate from this analysis.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 30 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Self-Distillation Zero: Self-Revision Turns Binary Rewards into Dense Supervision
papers.description: After training on verified self-revisions, SD-Zero samples generator responses and uses a reviser conditioned on each response and its binary reward to provide token-level targets. The reviser is frozen between synchronizations; the method requires a binary verifier and successful revision traces.
papers.objective: First, maximize the likelihood of verified revision traces under revision and generation prompts. Then minimize student-to-reviser token-level reverse KL on current student responses; the binary reward conditions the reviser.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 11 Jun 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Lightning OPD: Efficient Post-Training for Large Reasoning Models with Offline On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Lightning OPD caches teacher scores on initial-student rollouts and reuses them during student-only optimization. Its experiments compare refresh costs and cross-stage teacher pairings, without establishing that arbitrary cached supervision is equivalent to fresh OPD.
papers.objective: Supervised fine-tuning by maximum likelihood, followed by advantage-weighted policy-gradient updates on fixed reference rollouts, using clipped, stop-gradient teacher-minus-student sampled-token log-probability advantages.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 26 Sep 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
papers.description: This study compares teacher preparation, supervised cold starts, and prompt formats in mathematical-reasoning distillation. Its cold-start control fixes the subsequent teacher and prompt set; a separate experiment changes only the prompt template. Token overlap is a diagnostic rather than a universal test of transferable capability.
papers.objective: Bounded analyses of teacher choice, cold-start initialization, prompt-template alignment, and continuation behavior. The paper’s normalized top-k KL and its public probability-weighted log-ratio implementation are distinct update definitions.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 14 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 15 Apr 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: π-Play: Multi-Agent Self-Play via Privileged Self-Distillation without External Data
papers.description: In search-agent self-play, an examiner constructs questions and their search paths; a path-conditioned teacher supervises unprivileged student rollouts while the student also learns from outcome rewards. The teacher tracks the student by moving average, and evaluation is limited to search tasks.
papers.objective: The student combines clipped group-relative policy updates from answer-correctness rewards, reference-policy KL regularization, and per-token student-to-stop-gradient-teacher reverse KL on student rollouts; the teacher follows a moving average of student weights.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 25 May 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: TIP: Token Importance in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: TIP studies which positions in student-generated rollouts warrant distillation, selecting tokens using student entropy and teacher–student disagreement. Entropy alone misses confident disagreements; the combined selector retains them, but disagreement does not establish that the teacher’s preferred continuation is correct.
papers.objective: Minimize student-to-teacher reverse KL at selected token positions on student rollouts; a separate confident-disagreement diagnostic uses teacher-to-student forward KL for selection.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 21 May 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: The Illusion of Certainty: Decoupling Capability and Calibration in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: CaOPD examines how privileged-context self-teaching can transfer unjustified confidence alongside task behavior. It replaces verbalized confidence in the training completion and teacher context with a verifier-based success estimate from student rollouts, then distills on the revised completion; this requires parseable confidence and additional training rollouts.
papers.objective: Minimize per-token student-to-privileged-self-teacher reverse KL on a revised student completion whose verbalized confidence is replaced by the verified success rate of student rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 Apr 2026]

papers.title: OPSDL: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Context Language Models
papers.description: OPSDL uses short-context predictions of the same model to guide responses generated from long context. Multi-scale RULER and LongBench V2 comparisons evaluate the full recipe, without isolating every data-construction component or establishing the claimed gradient guarantee.
papers.objective: Policy-gradient guidance from short-view versus long-view sampled-token log probabilities on student responses; precise shared-teacher gradient handling is not fully specified.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 19 Apr 2026]

papers.title: Distillation Traps and Guards: A Calibration Knob for LLM Distillability
papers.description: Distillability calibration modifies a teacher using task rewards, an original-teacher anchor, and a smaller proxy model before running student-side GKD. Opposite calibration directions produce different student outcomes under the tested recipe, without establishing universal protection against extraction.
papers.objective: Calibrate the teacher before student-rollout GKD
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 21 Apr 2026]

papers.title: Hybrid Policy Distillation for LLMs
papers.description: HPD is evaluated as offline-prefix initialization for a later rollout-based OPD stage. The study compares HPD and SFT starts and reports stronger subsequent OPD results from HPD, without making the offline HPD procedure itself an on-policy trajectory method.
papers.objective: Compare offline initializations for subsequent rollout-based OPD
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 22 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 8 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: DeepSeek-V4: Towards Highly Efficient Million-Token Context Intelligence
papers.description: DeepSeek-V4 consolidates domain specialists through weighted full-vocabulary reverse KL on student-generated trajectories. Its training system caches teacher hidden states and reconstructs logits while scheduling prediction heads by teacher index; this describes the report’s post-training application, with teacher selection tied to task context.
papers.objective: Weighted full-vocabulary reverse KL from the student to specialist teachers on student-sampled trajectories.

papers.title: TCOD: Exploring Temporal Curriculum in On-Policy Distillation for Multi-turn Autonomous Agents
papers.description: TCOD addresses rising divergence across turns in interactive distillation by gradually extending the student’s training horizon. One variant lengthens student-generated prefixes; another starts student suffixes after successful teacher-executed prefixes, which require pre-collected trajectories and do not contribute gradients.
papers.objective: Minimize teacher-to-student KL on student-executed turns, initially over short prefixes or suffixes and then over a progressively longer interaction horizon; teacher-executed prefix turns receive no gradient.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 Apr 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: PAINT: Partial-Solution Adaptive Interpolated Training for Self-Distilled Reasoners
papers.description: PAINT studies how much reference-solution context a fixed self-teacher should receive when supervising student rollouts. Its masking-only comparisons vary overlap-dependent disclosure and block placement with target interpolation disabled, favoring moderate suffix masking in the tested Qwen3-1.7B setup.
papers.objective: Clipped forward-KL self-distillation under partial reference-solution context; the retained comparison concerns masking-only variants. The full method additionally proposes sparse energy interpolation.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Apr 2026]

papers.title: Co-Evolving Policy Distillation
papers.description: CoPD alternates capability-specific reward-based training with bidirectional distillation between evolving branches, each learning from its own rollouts scored by another branch. The evaluated consolidation covers text and image reasoning, with a separate three-branch setting adding video.
papers.objective: Capability-specific GRPO with verifiable rewards, interleaved with cross-branch updates that use the teacher-minus-student log probability of each sampled token as an advantage.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 29 Apr 2026]

papers.title: Beyond SFT-to-RL: Pre-alignment via Black-Box On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal RL
papers.description: PRISM inserts an adversarial pre-alignment stage between multimodal SFT and verifiable-reward RL, using separate perception and reasoning discriminators. Stage and discriminator comparisons support this teacher-mediated training recipe without establishing exact distribution matching or complete correction of rollout shift.
papers.objective: Discriminator-rewarded pre-alignment before multimodal RL
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 30 Apr 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 Jun 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Learn where to Click from Yourself: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
papers.description: GUI-SD compares privileged visual interfaces for GUI grounding. Its box-and-hint condition yields higher student grounding accuracy than textual coordinates despite lower teacher accuracy, showing that teacher accuracy alone does not determine transfer utility in the tested setting.
papers.objective: Analysis of visual versus textual privileged teacher inputs on student-generated coordinate predictions; the interface comparison is distinct from claims about the full weighting and EMA recipe.

papers.title: Healthcare AI GYM for Medical Agents
papers.description: TT-OPD combines GRPO with turn-normalized reverse-KL supervision from an outcome-conditioned EMA teacher on student-generated medical-agent trajectories. Component comparisons examine teacher updates, privileged hints, and length control, while reporting inconsistencies limit quantitative stability claims.
papers.objective: Turn-normalized reverse KL plus GRPO
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 1 May 2026]

papers.title: MAD-OPD: Breaking the Ceiling in On-Policy Distillation via Multi-Agent Debate
papers.description: MAD-OPD uses a confidence-weighted sum of losses to debate-conditioned teachers. Agent training uses sampled actions on ToolACE step instances; complete histories need not come from the current student. Debate alone helps code but slightly lowers the agentic ablation average, while confidence weighting helps both.
papers.objective: A post-debate-confidence-weighted sum of per-teacher token divergences: symmetric Jensen–Shannon divergence for agentic tasks or student-to-teacher reverse KL for code; agentic losses sum over sampled steps.

papers.title: Multilingual Safety Alignment via Self-Distillation
papers.description: The on-policy MSD variant uses a frozen teacher initialized from the same model, conditioned on a parallel English query and safety-reasoning instruction, to supervise student-generated prefixes through weighted reverse KL. Its DPSW weights combine teacher confidence with student disagreement; high weight is not a certificate of causal safety relevance.
papers.objective: Minimize reverse token KL from student to teacher, weighted using teacher confidence and student disagreement; only the student receives gradients. The on-policy variant samples student responses, while the off-policy variant samples teacher responses.

papers.title: Uni-OPD: Unifying On-Policy Distillation with a Dual-Perspective Recipe
papers.description: Uni-OPD combines offline difficulty balancing and batch-level correctness balancing with outcome calibration of trajectory-average teacher–student log-ratio returns. Each calibrated return is broadcast to the trajectory’s token advantages; component ablations examine the combined recipe.
papers.objective: A student policy-gradient loss uses teacher–student token log-probability gaps aggregated into trajectory returns, with outcome-guided margin masking or shifting; difficulty and correctness balancing select training data.

papers.title: Preference-Based Self-Distillation: Beyond KL Matching via Reward Regularization
papers.description: PBSD learns teacher-referenced preferences between privileged-teacher responses and current student samples. Its 8B experiments compare this sequence-preference route with token-level self-distillation; it is an adjacent transfer method rather than direct student-prefix distribution matching.
papers.objective: Teacher-referenced pairwise logistic loss on privileged-teacher and current-student response pairs.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 6 May 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 21 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Near-Policy: Accelerating On-Policy Distillation via Asynchronous Generation and Selective Packing
papers.description: Near-Policy Distillation periodically collects student responses, filters them by teacher–student difficulty discrepancy, and packs retained sequences for teacher scoring and supervised learner updates. Because generation and optimization are decoupled, sampled states can lag behind the current student rather than remain strictly on-policy.
papers.objective: Minimize a weighted combination of cross-entropy on retained student responses and teacher-to-student KL over the teacher’s top-k token support.

papers.title: Hindsight Compacts but Does Not Repair: Rethinking On-Policy Self-Distillation in Reasoning Models
papers.description: In mathematical reasoning, this study applies hindsight-conditioned self-distillation separately to correct and incorrect student rollouts to distinguish compaction from repair. Correct-only training shortens responses while largely preserving accuracy; incorrect-only training degrades accuracy, limiting claims that hindsight reliably repairs failed reasoning.
papers.objective: Token-level reverse KL from the student to a reflection-conditioned self-teacher on student-generated prefixes; correctness labels select diagnostic rollout subsets rather than supplying a reward.

papers.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation: Bridging Exploitation and Imitation at the Token Level
papers.description: On student-generated reasoning prefixes, AOPD retains log-probability-gap-weighted policy-gradient reinforcement for positive-advantage tokens but replaces non-positive updates with teacher-top-K forward-KL guidance, allowing unsampled alternatives to receive gradients. Its evaluations chiefly concern teacher–student mathematical-reasoning distillation, not self-distillation.

papers.title: UniSD: Towards a Unified Self-Distillation Framework for Large Language Models
papers.description: UniSD compares self-distillation variants using EMA targets, contrastive supervision, representation matching, and divergence clipping. Task-dependent results inform comparison of these components; they do not establish a benefit from the sequence-agreement scalar that cancels under the stated normalization.
papers.objective: Context-conditioned distribution matching on student rollouts, with variant-specific auxiliary losses; cited comparisons exclude the disputed sequence-agreement contribution.

papers.title: HyperEyes: Dual-Grained Efficiency-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Parallel Multimodal Search Agents
papers.description: HyperEyes trains a multimodal search agent with an adaptive trajectory-level reward for tool use and external-teacher token correction on failed student rollouts. Its parallel grounded-search action also changes; OPD is enabled for the smaller variant, so full-system results cannot isolate distillation.
papers.objective: Group-relative policy optimization using correctness, format, and adaptive tool-use rewards, combined with token-level external-teacher correction on failed student rollouts.

papers.title: LiteGUI: Distilling Compact GUI Agents with Reinforcement Learning
papers.description: LiteGUI distills on student-generated GUI outputs while giving the teacher a matched, human-verified valid action unavailable to the student, then applies dual-level reinforcement learning for planning and execution. Guidance and action rewards depend on a finite annotated set that can miss valid actions.
papers.objective: Reverse-KL distillation from a teacher conditioned on valid-action guidance, followed by group-relative policy optimization with model-evaluated subtask-planning and multi-solution action-matching rewards.

papers.title: SimCT: Recovering Lost Supervision for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: SimCT compares teacher and student on shared tokens plus short text continuations jointly expressible under different tokenizers, using student-generated prefixes and retaining the reverse-KL OPD loss. Its normalized candidate scores are not a probability-preserving mapping of all continuations.
papers.objective: Reverse KL between teacher and student distributions formed from normalized scores over shared tokens and minimally aligned continuation units on student-generated prefixes.

papers.title: SOD: Step-wise On-policy Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
papers.description: SOD addresses tool-call errors that shift later reasoning contexts by weighting each step’s sampled-token teacher–student log-likelihood signal according to changes in their discrepancy, alongside outcome-based reinforcement learning. Tool observations are excluded from the distillation loss; the discrepancy score is a proxy, not full token KL.
papers.objective: Group-relative policy optimization on outcome rewards plus step-weighted, sampled-token student-minus-teacher log-likelihood terms on student-generated tool-use trajectories.

papers.title: Prune-OPD: Efficient and Reliable On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Reasoning
papers.description: Prune-OPD weights teacher supervision by prefix compatibility and adjusts the next batch’s response budget. Reported time–accuracy comparisons differ between low- and high-compatibility pairs; they do not isolate compatibility selection from supervision quantity.
papers.objective: Compatibility-weighted teacher log-ratio updates on student prefixes with batch-level adjustment of subsequent rollout length.

papers.title: KL for a KL: On-Policy Distillation with Control Variate Baseline
papers.description: vOPD subtracts a detached, action-independent estimate of the per-token negative reverse KL as a baseline for the sampled-token policy-gradient update. Its top-k variant approximates the baseline rather than truncating the distillation objective; the study evaluates token-level reasoning distillation, not sequence-level objectives.
papers.objective: Sampled-token policy-gradient optimization of the teacher-minus-student log-probability reward, after subtracting a detached per-token negative reverse-KL baseline.

papers.title: The Extrapolation Cliff in On-Policy Distillation of Near-Deterministic Structured Outputs
papers.description: This study varies reward extrapolation and training duration in OPD for near-deterministic structured outputs. It finds abrupt losses of parsing validity despite comparatively stable ranking among valid outputs, while the proposed closed-form clipping threshold is not established by the reported implementation.

papers.title: Training with Harnesses: On-Policy Harness Self-Distillation for Complex Reasoning
papers.description: OPHSD prepares teacher context through a dynamic reasoning harness and supervises direct student rollouts with a frozen initial teacher. Comparisons with static privileged context evaluate the complete preparation recipe, including additional harness computation.

papers.title: Reasoning Compression with Mixed-Policy Distillation
papers.description: The student generates a reasoning trace, which a larger teacher rewrites concisely; the student then matches teacher token distributions on the rewritten trace. The training contexts are therefore not the original student prefixes, and the objective does not enforce answer correctness.
papers.objective: Minimize student-to-teacher token-level KL divergence on teacher-compressed student trajectories.

papers.title: CoDistill-GRPO: A Co-Distillation Recipe for Efficient Group Relative Policy Optimization
papers.description: Two models train jointly with group-relative policy updates: the smaller model receives a scalar distillation reward derived from the larger model, while the larger model reuses smaller-model rollouts with importance reweighting. Early rollouts can include larger-model hints; this is not reciprocal token-level distillation.

papers.title: Test-Time Speculation
papers.description: During speculative decoding, the draft model adapts within a generation using target-model distributions already computed to verify its proposed tokens. Position-weighted distillation includes a penalty against drifting from the previous draft; gradient updates add serving-time work even though the target remains unchanged.

papers.title: Crosslingual On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning
papers.description: COPSD trains on reasoning generated from low-resource-language problems, using a frozen self-teacher with privileged English translations and reference solutions. Experiments use full-vocabulary reverse KL on the same student prefixes; only the student is updated, and training requires English reference solutions.
papers.objective: Minimize full-vocabulary student-to-teacher reverse KL on student-generated prefixes in the experimental implementation, with a frozen privileged self-teacher and gradients only through the student.

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation with Best-of-N Teacher Rollout Selection
papers.description: BRTS supplements student-prefix distillation with a teacher-prefix branch selected for answer correctness and compatibility with the student. A recovery comparison supports answer-guided teacher resampling on difficult prompts, while the independent value of the compatibility tie-breaker remains unisolated.
papers.objective: Joint student-context and selected teacher-context distillation
