papers.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
papers.description: For open-ended tasks, a coach turns rubric assessments of policy-generated responses into reusable textual advice that conditions a teacher for token-level reverse-KL distillation along student rollouts. The coach supplies context rather than token probabilities, and the teacher may be frozen or iteratively updated.
papers.objective: An unnormalized reverse-KL sum over the student's top-256 tokens toward an advice-conditioned teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Solar Open 2 Technical Report
papers.description: Solar Open 2 documents routed full-vocabulary OPD using hidden-state transport and tiled logit reconstruction. Teacher-indexed caching and on-demand pool loading reduce tensor residency and transfer demands, without establishing proportional end-to-end speedups.
papers.objective: Full-vocabulary reverse-KL consolidation without outcome rewards
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 22 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 24 Jul 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation via Byte-Prefix Marginalization
papers.description: BPM maps teacher probability mass to student byte-prefix cells and a residual cell, with a separate stop-token bridge. Its exactness depends on stated tokenization assumptions; realized-path spanning corrections lower-bound the full marginal. Alignment masks and divergence choices affect the reported cross-tokenizer results.
papers.objective: Generalized Jensen–Shannon divergence between projected student probabilities and byte-prefix teacher targets at included content positions, with forward-KL stop-token bridge supervision.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 24 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Self-Boosting Vision-Language Models with Noisy Student On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: On corrupted-image student rollouts, a vision-language model matches its own stopped-gradient clean-image token distribution using reverse KL. The teacher view shares the student’s parameters rather than supplying external answers; the method depends on visual input corruption.
papers.objective: Reverse KL from the corrupted-image student distribution to the stopped-gradient clean-image self-teacher distribution at student-generated prefixes; sampling is not backpropagated through.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 31 Jul 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Outcome-Confounded Local Supervision in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This diagnostic separates sampled-token teacher–student discrepancy from trajectory correctness. In independent threshold runs, most incorrect responses contain predominantly low-discrepancy tokens. Local agreement therefore does not locate the decisive error; the analysis does not prove a general impossibility of credit assignment.
papers.objective: Diagnostic binning of sampled-token divergence by final-answer correctness; training probes compare ordinary distillation, masking failed responses, and sequence-level contrast.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 Jul 2026]

papers.title: The Physics of Multi-Turn Long-Horizon Planning: From Pre-training to Post-training via Single- and Multi-Teacher On-Policy Agentic Distillation
papers.description: This synthetic-planning study compares OPD and outcome-reward training across data quality and horizon. Its idealized teacher’s described training source includes evaluation instantiations, whereas the student uses separate pools. The evidence concerns this oracle-teacher setting.
papers.objective: Teacher-supervised token updates on student interactive trajectories, compared with group-relative outcome optimization in controlled synthetic tasks.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Pass the Baton: Trajectory-Relayed On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Relay-OPD detects when the teacher favors a reflection token absent from the student’s leading options, then inserts short, budgeted teacher continuations into student rollouts. The student resumes when the budget permits, and distillation uses the resulting mixed trajectories; evaluation focuses on mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: Reverse-KL-style sampled-token policy-gradient distillation using teacher-versus-student log-probability advantages on generated relay tokens.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: W2S-OPD forms a proxy teacher by adding the logit difference between weaker positive and negative sources to a frozen copy of the student’s base model, then distills it on student-generated rollouts. The tested contrasts and evaluations concern mathematical reasoning and code generation.
papers.objective: Reverse KL after restricting both student and synthetic proxy-teacher distributions to the proxy teacher’s top-32 support and renormalizing.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: DASH-OPD: Discrepancy-Aware Switching with Hysteresis for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: DASH-OPD accumulates drift and recovery evidence to alternate student and teacher execution, applying different losses to each source. Updated controls isolate recovery and evidence accumulation with matched tuning budgets. Fewer switches and teacher turns are measured execution properties, not a demonstrated end-to-end speedup.
papers.objective: Reverse KL on valid response tokens in student turns and forward KL on valid response tokens in teacher turns, with a teacher-turn weight.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 31 Jul 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 26 Sep 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: SAF-OPD: Stable Advantage Fusion for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: SAF-OPD sparsifies, compresses, and schedules teacher log-ratio advantages before combining them with verifier-based GRPO advantages. Its complete recipe improves over the tested unit-coefficient fusion across three student scales and two domains, without establishing superiority over tuned fixed coefficients.
papers.objective: GRPO plus sparsified, compressed, and scheduled teacher log-ratio advantages
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 31 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Adaptive FastOPD: Progress-Aware Rollout Horizon Expansion for Efficient On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Adaptive FastOPD expands student rollout horizons when teacher–student signals near the current boundary plateau relative to their starting values and enough rollouts use the available length. It retains token-level teacher supervision; evaluation covers mathematical reasoning with two teacher–student pairs.
papers.objective: A clipped policy surrogate on student-visited prefixes, using student-selected token candidates and student-probability-weighted teacher–student log-probability differences.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 31 Jul 2026]

papers.title: Distill Where You Fail: Recovering Learning Signals of Negative RL-Groups from Adaptive Teacher Guidance
papers.description: This study tests teacher supervision for all-failure rollout groups. Its sequential ablation reports a gain from teacher-based advantage weighting before adding token selection or teacher-response SFT, providing a bounded comparison for recovering a signal when group-relative outcome advantages vanish.
papers.objective: Analysis of negative-group OPD and teacher-based advantage weighting alongside GRPO; the complete RSTG variant additionally selects tokens and uses teacher-response SFT.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 1 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Distill What the Student Can See: Fisher-Projected On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models
papers.description: FP-OPD estimates a vision-language student’s local visual-response space with perturbation probes, then Fisher-projects the teacher correction to construct targets for student-generated prefixes. It models local reachability rather than global representational capacity, and the probes require additional forward passes.
papers.objective: Full-vocabulary token-level reverse KL from the student distribution to a detached, Fisher-projected target on student-generated prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 6 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Is More Privileged Information Better? From Solution Traces to Problem-Solving Structure in Self-Distilled Reasoning
papers.description: PS-OPSD compares complete reference solutions with structured problem-space guidance for the teacher while retaining the same student-prefix distillation objective. Mismatched and path-corrupted guidance test content, and checkpoint-specific results qualify claims of uniform improvement.
papers.objective: Student-prefix distribution matching to a privileged self-teacher with alternative reference-solution representations; comparisons vary teacher context.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Aug 2026]

papers.title: DAPD: Dual-Anchored Policy Distillation
papers.description: DAPD addresses privilege illusion in on-policy self-distillation with a trainable, self-conditioned bridge. It aligns reference and rollout behavior along inference-context and privileged-context paths in both guidance directions, while retaining the original privileged-teacher supervision rather than replacing it entirely.
papers.objective: A weighted combination of three directed token-distribution divergences: detached cross-conditioned targets supervise unconditioned and self-conditioned predictions, and detached unconditioned targets supervise self-conditioned predictions; the paths are applied in both completion directions.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 13 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: PCSD: Persistent Consistency for Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.description: PCSD aggregates signed teacher-student log-probability gaps over local windows to modulate an auxiliary update on student-generated trajectories. Pointwise comparisons and component ablations support the tested recipe without establishing teacher-reliability detection or exact distribution matching.
papers.objective: Teacher-gap-weighted auxiliary NLL plus GRPO
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Look Ahead Before You Distill: Future Trajectory Validation of Teacher Guidance for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: FutureBridge-OPD selects a student-controlled turn with weak sampled teacher support, substitutes a teacher action, and compares paired student continuations before retaining the bridge for distillation. This validation uses future teacher-preferred-token density, not task reward, and builds on a curriculum initialized from successful trajectories.
papers.objective: Sampled teacher–student log-probability advantages drive distillation; an accepted teacher bridge receives a detached-advantage-weighted student log-likelihood update. Acceptance requires its student continuation to have a higher teacher-preferred-token fraction than the original continuation.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 5 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Self-Improving Large Language Models via Progressive Experience Evolution
papers.description: SPEE consolidates experience from successful and failed trajectories into privileged self-teacher context for distillation on student-generated prefixes, followed by GRPO. Its reported single-round results support the combined experience-distillation recipe without establishing sustained improvement across repeated training cycles.
papers.objective: Experience-conditioned reverse-KL self-distillation followed by GRPO
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 4 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Rubrics as Privileged Information for Open-Ended Generation
papers.description: For open-ended responses, a self-teacher sees natural-language rubrics while the student generates prefixes without them; clipped token-level reverse KL transfers the teacher’s distribution rather than a scalar rubric reward. The main full-finetuning variant uses an EMA teacher, while an adapter variant uses a frozen-base teacher.
papers.objective: Clipped per-token student-to-rubric-conditioned-teacher reverse KL on student-generated rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Aug 2026]

papers.title: SMOPD: Multi-Reward Reinforcement Learning via Specialize-and-Merge Online Policy Distillation
papers.description: SMOPD merges reward-specialized teachers on student-generated prefixes and combines distillation with a balanced task-reward anchor. Its explicitly defined sampled reverse-KL variant supports the merging recipe, while the default candidate-pooling target and claims about divergence direction require qualification.
papers.objective: Multi-teacher matching plus balanced GDPO reward anchoring
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 4 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 21 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: SPOT: Sparse Probing and Outcome Calibration for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: SPOT ranks student-generated positions for sparse probing using teacher entropy, top-candidate mass and student–teacher mismatch. Verifier-scored student continuations then tilt a teacher-anchored target for an additional local distillation loss, applied only at selected positions with a positive-reward branch.
papers.objective: Baseline student-to-teacher reverse KL on student-generated prefixes, plus a local loss fitting verifier-outcome-tilted teacher targets at selected positions with a positive-reward candidate.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 5 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 17 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Privileged, but Biased: How PI-Conditioned Teachers Break Self-Distillation
papers.description: This analysis tests privileged-information self-distillation without a reward term. On the harder tasks studied, a teacher conditioned on one solution favors that path, while token-level loss falls without corresponding accuracy gains; the study does not evaluate reward–distillation hybrids.
papers.objective: Analyze reward-free, per-token student–self-teacher divergence on student rollouts, using Jensen–Shannon divergence in the main runs and forward KL in the tested variant.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 5 Aug 2026]

papers.title: OPD-V: Visual On-Policy Self-Distillation with Modality Balance
papers.description: OPD-V uses an EMA self-teacher on an evidence-centered crop to supervise student rollouts from the original image. A positive log-probability margin over a masked-crop teacher both gates and weights Jensen–Shannon matching. The margin is a relative visual-context proxy, not a certificate of correctness or modality balance.
papers.objective: Positive-margin-weighted JSD on the student top-100 vocabulary plus a tail bucket, averaged over valid response tokens, with detached capped importance weights and rollout correction.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 5 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 6 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Capek 0.5: An Execution-Centric Vision-Language Model for Embodied Intelligence
papers.description: Capek combines specialist weight merging with routed teacher matching on student-generated prefixes. Its consolidation comparisons support complementary roles for TIES initialization and subsequent OPD, with uneven retention across individual capabilities.
papers.objective: TIES initialization followed by routed specialist distillation
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Aug 2026]

papers.title: MemOPD: On-Policy Distillation through Memory State Alignment for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.description: For compact-memory agents, this method reconstructs each student invocation’s tokens, positions and causal visibility before a frozen teacher scores sampled actions, avoiding supervision under an unvisited flattened-history state. It combines teacher distribution matching with task-reward PPO; end-to-end training is tested on retrieval tasks.
papers.objective: Minimize full-vocabulary student-to-teacher reverse KL at reconstructed sampled-action states alongside a clipped PPO objective for final task reward.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Trajectory-Relative Hindsight Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.description: On student-generated multi-turn interactions, this method scores realized tokens with and without their turn’s post-action outcome, then uses signed probability gaps to guide updates. It normalizes gap magnitudes across turns to allocate dense hindsight feedback alongside outcome-based GRPO; evaluation covers two interactive environments.
papers.objective: Add a detached, signed log-probability-gap-weighted token policy-gradient loss, with trajectory-normalized turn weights and a scalar clamp, to the outcome-based GRPO loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Adaptive Supervised Anchoring for On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: SDS separates teacher-distribution matching on student-generated prefixes from supervised anchoring on canonical answer prefixes. Its fixed-weight variants provide evidence about this context separation, independently of the unspecified similarity operator used by the adaptive variant.
papers.objective: Student-prefix generalized JSD + fixed-weight canonical-prefix cross-entropy
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 11 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Matching Supervision to the Student's Learning Capacity: A Unified Framework for On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: The method jointly adjusts soft token weights and how much reference context a privileged self-teacher sees while scoring student rollouts. A fixed learning-difficulty budget drives both controls through online updates; it is a capacity model, not a measured or automatically changing student-capacity limit.
papers.objective: A normalized, softly token-weighted forward KL from the privileged teacher to the student on student rollouts; difficulty-based updates adjust token weights and teacher context exposure against a fixed budget.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Aug 2026]

papers.title: PAST: Privileged Adaptation from Complete Student Trajectories for On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: PAST adapts a hindsight-conditioned teacher using completed student trajectories, then distills it on original student prefixes. A fixed-step factorial comparison supports the combined recipe in the evaluated setting, without a universal guarantee for future-conditioned supervision.
papers.objective: Clipped teacher-to-student forward KL on original student prefixes after trajectory-conditioned teacher adaptation.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 9 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Reading is not Reasoning: Bridging the Agentic Policy Gap in Vision-Text Compression
papers.description: CAPS first trains a visual-history student on successful text-policy responses, then combines environmental-reward training with forward-KL supervision from a frozen text-history self-teacher on student-visited states. The teacher receives the corresponding textual history, without ground-truth solutions; training requires paired history representations.
papers.objective: Offline next-token prediction of complete teacher responses, followed by group-relative environmental-reward training plus masked, capped, full-vocabulary teacher-to-student forward KL on student-generated prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 9 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Privileged Solutions or Context-Induced Teacher Behavior? Dissecting On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: This diagnostic study replaces the target problem’s reference solution with another mathematics problem’s worked solution in the self-teacher’s context, while preserving student rollouts and the distillation objective. The results challenge a purely answer-transfer explanation but do not identify a unique causal mechanism.
papers.objective: A clipped teacher-to-student forward-KL surrogate on student-generated prefixes, with gradients only through the student; the experimental change is the teacher-only worked-solution context.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Privileged Likelihood Is Not Automatically Value: Three Checks for Token Credit in On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: This analysis asks whether token likelihood changes under hindsight feedback track task success, whether feedback written about the scored rollout creates self-dependence, and what token-weighted updates reinforce. Its mathematics experiments show a failure case, not that every privileged likelihood signal lacks outcome value.
papers.objective: Audits teacher token-log-likelihood contrasts under helpful versus incorrect hindsight feedback, including feedback from other same-problem rollouts, and compares training using those scores with outcome-only training.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 25 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: WDL-OPD: Weak-Driven On-Policy Distillation via Mixture-Constrained Co-Training
papers.description: An anchor policy supplies all rollouts while a trainable auxiliary evaluates the same prefixes; both receive gradients from matching their geometric token-distribution mixture to a frozen teacher. The reported stability evidence is descriptive because initialization, curriculum, and compute are not fully matched across comparisons.
papers.objective: Token-mean reverse KL from the normalized geometric mixture of anchor and auxiliary distributions to the frozen teacher, on the anchor’s selected top-token support; gradients update both policies.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 3 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: SR-OPSD: Self-Referenced On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: On student-generated prefixes, SR-OPSD geometrically mixes a privileged-context self-teacher with a frozen initial-policy reference, then minimizes forward Rényi divergence from that target to the student. Its variational characterization applies to fixed rollout contexts, not the full moving-policy dynamics.
papers.objective: Minimize forward Rényi divergence from the stopped, reference-anchored token target to the student distribution on student-generated prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Distill Skills into Weights, Not Prompts: Abstract Skills as Privileged Signals for On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.description: SKALD scores question-only student rollouts with a shared-parameter teacher given answer-filtered abstract skill cards, combining gated, annealed tilted cross-entropy with group-relative reward optimization. Its fixed gate estimates initial teacher advantage, not whether the moving teacher remains better throughout training.
papers.objective: Combine group-normalized reward policy gradients with skill-teacher cross-entropy on student prefixes, initially tilted against low-student-likelihood tokens and activated by a fixed empirical gate.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Mismatch Matters: On-Policy Distillation Beyond Token Agreement
papers.description: TIDE diagnoses repetitive rollouts where local teacher agreement masks failure, then independently gates severe student-excess and student-deficit positions. It uses bounded Hellinger-shaped sampled-token suppression and teacher top-K cross-entropy to recover missing mass; its experiments concern mathematical reasoning with fixed external teachers.
papers.objective: Jointly apply a detached, Hellinger-shaped policy-gradient signal to selected sampled excess tokens and teacher top-K cross-entropy to independently selected deficit positions.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Open-MOPD: Diagnosing and Fixing Capability Imbalance in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Open-MOPD studies uneven transfer from oracle-routed domain teachers to a shared student and adjusts domain token shares and remaining-gap weights. Across reused rollout minibatches, it refreshes student-dependent rewards while retaining teacher scores; sampled states and routing are not refreshed.
papers.objective: Use PPO with a domain-weighted scalar reward built from teacher-minus-student log probabilities on the student's top token candidates, refreshing its student-dependent term for each inner update.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 19 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
papers.description: GC-OPD separately normalizes verifier rewards and mean teacher–student token scores within student rollout groups. It distributes their signed difference across tokens while retaining the original distillation advantage; the correction vanishes when either group-level signal has negligible variation.
papers.objective: A clipped token-level policy objective using detached teacher–student log-probability advantages plus a token-weighted, signed verifier–teacher disagreement residual.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 19 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Beyond Imitation: Filtering On-Policy Distillation by Reasoning Progress
papers.description: R2-OPD estimates reasoning progress from student continuations, merges adjacent spans with consistent progress signs, and masks reverse-KL supervision where progress and teacher-disagreement rankings conflict. Progress controls which tokens receive distillation; responses without usable estimates retain their original supervision.
papers.objective: Minimize student-to-teacher token-distribution reverse KL on retained tokens, using estimated reasoning progress only to select spans for masking.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 19 Aug 2026]

papers.title: SecOPD: Mitigating Adaptive Prompt Injections by On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: For indirect prompt-injection defense, this application samples student responses to attacked inputs and scores each token with a frozen initialization model given the corresponding clean input, using detached token advantages for policy updates. It assumes trusted instructions and untrusted data are distinguishable.
papers.objective: Update the student on sampled attacked-input tokens using detached advantages equal to clean-context teacher log probability minus attacked-context rollout-policy log probability.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 21 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Hints, Critics, and Teachers: Prior Injection for Sparse-Reward RL in Vision-Language Math Reasoning
papers.description: In a vision-language mathematical-reasoning comparison, one validation slice reverses training-arm rankings relative to cross-domain transfer, whereas a harder slice correlates positively. The study illustrates validation-set sensitivity; single-seed results and differing answer access limit method rankings.
papers.objective: Comparison of validation-slice rankings and cross-domain performance across eleven training arms.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 22 Aug 2026]

papers.title: OPDSearch+: On-Policy Distillation with RL Refinement for Search-Augmented Reasoning
papers.description: OPDSearch+ first distills a frozen teacher on student trajectories that include live retrieval, then refines the student with outcome-based RL. Comparisons with offline preparation, RL alone, and simultaneous training support the sequential recipe in the tested search setting.
papers.objective: Retrieval-state distillation followed by teacher-free GRPO
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Aug 2026]

papers.title: On-policy Distillation with Verifiable Reward
papers.description: On student-generated reasoning trajectories, this method gates each sampled token’s teacher–student log-probability signal by verified correctness, retaining updates that reinforce correct responses or suppress incorrect ones. Its group-relative variant uses the sign, not the magnitude, of the group advantage; the reported tests concern mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: Negative sampled-token log likelihood weighted by a correctness-signed, ReLU-gated teacher–student log-probability ratio; the group-relative variant gates using the sign of the group advantage.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 Sep 2026 (this version, v4)]

papers.title: D$^3$-MOPD: Dynamic Domain ScheDuling for Efficient Multi-Teacher Distillation
papers.description: D3-MOPD adjusts domain prompt sampling using each domain’s remaining normalized reverse KL and recent KL descent during multi-teacher distillation on student rollouts. The reverse-KL update stays unchanged, but the default scheduler can sharply reduce sampling when a domain’s KL temporarily rebounds.
papers.objective: Minimize per-domain student-to-teacher reverse KL on student-generated trajectories, with domain sampling shares updated from normalized remaining KL and recent KL descent.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: CataOPD: Catalytic On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Model Reasoning
papers.description: CataOPD first attempts unguided recovery of all-failed rollout groups, then uses teacher hints to help the student produce verified training targets. Ablations support recovery, guidance, and guided-versus-unaided token weighting, while the additional sampling has a separate training cost.
papers.objective: Verified student-target internalization plus outcome-based RL
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 25 Aug 2026]

papers.title: A Token-Level Analysis of Sampled-Token Reverse-KL On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This study analyzes logit gradients of a directly backpropagated sampled-token squared-log-ratio loss and tests detached surprise weights in mathematical reasoning. The analysis holds sampled prefixes fixed; experiments leave unresolved how much improvement comes from exact surprise alignment versus more general nonuniform weighting.
papers.objective: Directly minimize the token-mean squared teacher–student sampled-token log-probability gap on student rollouts; the tested variant multiplies each token loss by a detached, bounded student-surprise weight.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 26 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 27 Aug 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Recovering General Capabilities via Uncertainty-Calibrated Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: For recovery after domain specialization, this method samples anchor and exploratory student trajectories, retains exploratory ones with sufficient positive teacher–student signal, then probabilistically filters token updates by agreement with teacher endorsement. It is tested in role-playing and medical settings, not as a general retention guarantee.
papers.objective: A sampled-token, reverse-KL-style policy-gradient surrogate uses clipped, stop-gradient teacher-minus-student log-probability advantages; only trajectories passing the positive-advantage filter and token updates retained by the entropy-centered endorsement gate contribute.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 28 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Consolidating RLVR Capabilities Across Domains: A Deep Dive into Fusion Paradigms
papers.description: Using shared domain experts and data, this study compares weight merging, pooled reward training, and multi-teacher OPD. Domain retention and complete training costs distinguish the methods. The 4B pass@32 and held-out tests do not establish broader solution coverage than the base model.
papers.objective: The distillation arm minimizes token-level student-to-domain-teacher reverse KL at student-visited prefixes. Comparators combine expert task vectors or train on pooled prompts with domain-verifier rewards.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 27 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 18 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: SpikeOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Autoregressive Spiking Language Models
papers.description: SpikeOPD adapts a distilled spiking language model on its own generated prefixes, combining teacher distribution matching with an anchor to the initial distilled checkpoint and layerwise firing-rate constraints. Its stability findings concern the evaluated spiking students, not language-model architectures generally.
papers.objective: On detached student-generated prefixes, minimize full-vocabulary teacher-to-student KL, student-to-frozen-reference KL, and selected-layer firing-rate penalties against an interval and reference rates.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Aug 2026]

papers.title: When Teacher Guidance Misleads: Reward-Aligned On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: RA-OPD filters student trajectories when the sign of their aggregate teacher–student log-probability signal conflicts with a verified binary outcome. Retained trajectories receive sampled-token distillation updates. The rule requires outcome verification and selects complete trajectories, leaving their token-level rewards unchanged.
papers.objective: A binary outcome check masks entire trajectories; retained sampled tokens receive a policy-gradient surrogate weighted by stopped teacher-minus-student log probability.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 28 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Influence-Directed Distillation: Solving the Diversity Bottleneck in Sampled-Token On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: IDA-OPD estimates each sampled-token update’s local entropy effect, preserves entropy-expanding updates, and shrinks contracting advantages according to teacher–student disagreement. The entropy sign result assumes a local logit-space step; behavior under full model training is evaluated empirically.
papers.objective: A sampled-token policy-gradient surrogate uses stopped teacher-minus-student log-probability advantages, shrinking them at predicted entropy-contracting positions by sampled-token disagreement.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 30 Aug 2026]

papers.title: Does On-Policy Distillation Really Distill? From Noisy Teacher to Self-Improvement
papers.description: This study tests whether sampled-token OPD gains require teacher guidance, finding that answer-token advantage signs can conflict with verified correctness and that suppressing low-probability student tokens can reproduce gains in its tests. Its resulting self-adaptation method uses no teacher, so these findings do not establish a mechanism for full-distribution OPD.
papers.objective: For the teacher-free control, apply entropy-scaled negative policy-gradient advantages only to the lowest-log-probability fifth of student-sampled tokens; the analyzed OPD baseline uses sampled-token teacher-minus-student log-probability advantages.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 31 Aug 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 24 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Learn from Whoever Is Right: Answer-Verified Multi-Teacher Distillation for Multi-Domain LLMs
papers.description: MT-SDPO uses correct student peers as anchors and admits frozen teachers whose cached answers pass verification. Sanitized critiques condition a privileged moving-average self-teacher that supervises student tokens. The answer check does not certify subsequent critiques; evaluation uses multiple-choice science questions.
papers.objective: Masked, importance-weighted token-level Jensen–Shannon divergence between the student and a context-privileged, stop-gradient moving-average self-teacher.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Verify Before You Distill: Prompt-Level Teacher Gating for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Verifier-scored teacher probes estimate reliability for each prompt before its student rollouts receive supervision. A passing prompt uses token-level on-policy distillation; a failing one uses group-relative verifier rewards instead, with no blended update. The fallback yields no update when every student rollout has the same reward.
papers.objective: A clipped policy-gradient update selects either per-token teacher–student log-likelihood-gap advantages or group-centered verifier-reward advantages for each prompt.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 2 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Sequential Beats Joint: On the Interplay between On-Policy Distillation and RLVR
papers.description: This study compares distillation followed by verifier-reward reinforcement learning with joint updates. On logic and mathematics tasks, reverse-KL distillation expands coverage of teacher-supported solutions and subsequent reinforcement learning sharpens that support; this explanation is based on the evaluated training settings.
papers.objective: First minimize student-to-teacher reverse KL on student rollouts; then optimize group-relative verifier rewards with a clipped policy-gradient objective.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 4 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
papers.description: This study compares repeated distillation from very few queries with full-data training. A top-k configuration tests task performance; separate sampled-token runs measure semantic-cluster coverage and alignment rates. The coverage proxy does not measure visitation frequency or instructional value.
papers.objective: Reverse-KL alignment to teacher next-token distributions at student-visited prefixes, estimated using sampled-token or top-k corrections.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Extremely Sparse Supervision Incentivizes Reasoning Ability
papers.description: Sparse-OPD experiments restrict teacher supervision to a few selected tokens on each student trajectory. Random and extreme-signal selections reveal that dense supervision is not always necessary for the tested reasoning gains, while successful sparsification does not consistently reduce teacher-student KL or rollout cost.
papers.objective: Masked sampled-token teacher-log-ratio optimization
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 3 Sep 2026]

papers.title: What Matters in On-Policy Distillation? A Perspective on Data Efficiency and Data Selection
papers.description: This study selects mathematical prompts using teacher and student rollout accuracy, then distills on student-generated responses. Eight selected hard prompts and a random 1K subset both approach the 17K baseline in the reported configuration. Length-capping controls show a bounded selection effect, without isolating length as its sole cause.
papers.objective: Renormalized student-top-k reverse KL against teacher next-token distributions on student-generated prefixes.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 4 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 26 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation
papers.description: After a reward-based policy update, this method extrapolates from a trailing checkpoint in weight or logit space to form a refreshed teacher, then distills its token distributions into the student. Distillation reuses pre-update rollouts, making their contexts mildly off-policy for the updated student.
papers.objective: Outcome-reward policy-gradient update followed by Jensen–Shannon divergence to a stop-gradient extrapolated teacher on reused student rollouts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 4 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Teacher Should Think Ahead: Adaptive Continuations for Reliable On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: AC-OPD supplements sampled-token OPD on student rollouts with teacher continuations from selected prefix anchors. It adapts how many branch tokens receive cross-entropy supervision using uncertainty and path-divergence proxies; a shuffled-length control tests local length assignment. Candidate branches are generated before masking, so shorter supervision does not itself save teacher decoding.
papers.objective: Minimize a student-rollout policy-gradient surrogate weighted by stopped teacher-minus-student sampled-token log probabilities, plus cross-entropy on retained teacher-continuation tokens.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 6 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Teaching a Moving Student: Rethinking the Curriculum of On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: R-OPD follows the evolving student before switching to replayed initial-student trajectories when changes in mean gradients become comparable to minibatch variation. Its mathematics experiments examine when revisiting earlier states helps; replayed trajectories are not fresh samples from the current policy.
papers.objective: Teacher-guided distillation with a gradient-triggered switch from current-policy rollout collection to initial-policy replay.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 6 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 26 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Revisiting Complete Reasoning Traces for Post-Training
papers.description: A small OPD comparison tests masking the middle 20% of tokens or reasoning steps against unmasked supervision. Step masking gives the highest reported average, while MATH-500 declines, illustrating a setting-dependent tradeoff in supervision coverage.
papers.objective: OPD with token-level or reasoning-step-level middle-segment loss masks; the reported intervention removes the middle 20%.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 7 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Distillation as Probability Transport: Routed On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: On student-visited prefixes, the method pairs tokens with excess student probability with tokens underweighted relative to the teacher, then fits localized pairwise log-odds changes to consistent, bounded targets. Its routing uses a sparse shared token support and is evaluated on mathematical reasoning.
papers.objective: An excess-mass-weighted Huber loss fits sampled source-to-destination log-odds changes to targets derived from a shared bounded teacher potential; only current-student terms receive gradients.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Sep 2026]

papers.title: TV-Regulated OPD: Direction Matters in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: The paper tests whether sampled-token likelihood-gap magnitudes matter beyond their signs, then uses teacher-relative signs with conditional total variation to regulate overall update intensity. Its gradient interpretation concerns the on-policy signal with fixed state occupancy, not a full sequence-level derivative.
papers.objective: A detached teacher-relative sign weights each sampled token’s student log-probability, while conditional total variation regulates the global update scale.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 29 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: Miles v0.1: Production-Level Post-Training
papers.description: Miles integrates teacher log-probability scoring with configurable advantage estimators through served and in-process deployment paths. Its OPD contribution is the scoring and routing interface with explicit tokenizer and architecture constraints, while a five-step example demonstrates use without establishing a system speedup.
papers.objective: Sampled reverse-KL advantage shaping
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Video-MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Video Understanding
papers.description: Video-MOPD consolidates video-domain experts using routed teacher supervision on student rollouts. It compares the resulting model with direct averaging of the same experts and tests token-support choices. The full-pipeline results do not isolate data selection or establish equal-compute superiority.
papers.objective: Domain-routed teacher supervision on student-generated response prefixes following expert training and data selection.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 8 Sep 2026]

papers.title: CompassOPD: Cross-Family On-Policy Distillation via Within-Family Likelihood Shifts
papers.description: CompassOPD scores student-generated actions with a strong teacher and a weaker reference from the same family, transferring their likelihood shift rather than the cross-family offset. A frozen initial student anchors updates; the evaluated MoE variant obtains its reference by reducing expert activation.
papers.objective: A stopped-gradient advantage combines the teacher-versus-reference log-likelihood difference with a penalty for the sampled token’s log-likelihood change from the initial student; the student is updated with a policy-gradient loss.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 9 Sep 2026]

papers.title: KuaiRP Series Role-playing Models Technical Report
papers.description: KuaiRP restarts from the original base model to transfer a role-play specialist’s behavior and world knowledge in separate stages. It compares sampled-token policy-gradient distillation with teacher-top-k forward-KL training. Results include weak knowledge transfer under sampled-token updates and failures on the evaluated 9B model.
papers.objective: Two-stage transfer using sampled-token teacher log-ratio advantages for behavior and teacher-top-k forward KL for knowledge.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 10 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Data-Free On-Policy Distillation: How Far Can We Go Without External Data?
papers.description: Data-Free OPD has the teacher write questions without external seeds or correctness-based selection; extraction, format checks, and deduplication still apply. Student rollouts receive teacher token supervision. Reported peaks, fixed-initial-student coverage diagnostics, and inconsistent empty-prompt results delimit the few-question finding.
papers.objective: On student-generated states, a stopped-gradient, student-top-token-weighted teacher-minus-student log-probability signal weights the student log-likelihood update; the paper presents reverse KL as the underlying OPD objective.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 12 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 1 Oct 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Know When to Stop, Where to Restart: Accelerating Multi-Turn Agentic On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: STRIDE stops multi-turn student rollouts using cumulative teacher log-probability, then restarts from a cached student prefix selected by a likelihood threshold. Buffer ablations and measured time per step support the tested recipe; the threshold does not certify prefix correctness.
papers.objective: A stopped teacher-minus-student token log-probability signal weights a policy-gradient update on retained student-generated tokens, including the stopping turn; environment observations are masked out.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Lightning Weave: Improving the Accuracy-Efficiency Frontier of Reasoning Models through Capability Composition
papers.description: Lightning Weave combines aligned policy shifts into an explicit target on cached student states and fits a finite-support log-residual loss. Its composition comparisons favor joint target construction over data mixing and sequential application, while full-vocabulary KL identities do not transfer unchanged to the implemented surrogate.
papers.objective: Fit composed policy-shift targets on cached student prefixes
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 13 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 16 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: The method contrasts one privileged-vision teacher's predictions with a real image and a visual null under the same student-generated prefix, then distills a reconstructed target on that rollout. It addresses erroneous prefixes that can obscure visual correction; reflection tokens are an observed effect, not an explicit target.
papers.objective: Minimize a token-level divergence between the student and a target formed by tilting the privileged teacher's distribution toward its real-image-versus-null-image preference.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Beyond Token-Local Imitation: Reward-Compatible Temporal Credit Assignment for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: The paper analyzes why token-local distillation credit omits a token's effects on later prefixes, then proposes discounted future teacher credit mixed with verifiable outcome feedback. Its horizon-independent variance bound applies to a fixed discount below one under the paper's assumptions, not to undiscounted credit.
papers.objective: A policy-gradient surrogate using discounted future student–teacher log-ratio credit, with bounded mixing of that teacher-derived credit and a verifier's outcome reward.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 15 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 19 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: SEA-LION-v4.8: A Technical Report
papers.description: SEA-LION-v4.8 documents asynchronous OPD interleaved with SFT across concurrent agent environments. Token-level version tracking, staleness masking, and compressed teacher outputs specify its operating design, without an isolated comparison establishing a universal throughput advantage.
papers.objective: Asynchronous top-k teacher matching with interleaved SFT
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 16 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 18 Sep 2026 (this version, v3)]

papers.title: Trajectory Learnability for Offline On-Policy Distillation with Imperfect Teachers
papers.description: LWD estimates trajectory weights for cached student records by measuring how a reference student changes after learning from teacher-successful problems. Its comparisons favor graded retention over discarding every teacher-failed record, while code-side success labels indicate format validity rather than executable correctness.
papers.objective: Trajectory-weighted distillation on cached student states
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 16 Sep 2026]

papers.title: When EOS Tokens Disagree: Understanding Length Inflation in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This study traces some response-length inflation in sampled-token distillation to students and teachers preferring different tokens for the same stopping action. Aggregating equivalent termination tokens in the training signal mitigates that mismatch in single-turn math tests, but late-run inflation can remain.
papers.objective: Analyze detached sampled-token teacher-minus-student log-probability feedback and compare termination-handling corrections that align equivalent stopping tokens in the distillation signal.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 17 Sep 2026]

papers.title: GVPO++: Group Variance Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training and On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: GVPO++ matches group-centered teacher-student sequence log-probability differences on student-generated responses, allowing different tokenizers. Its distillation experiments and length-weight sweeps support sequence-level matching, with benefits that depend on the weighting choice.
papers.objective: Squared group-centered sequence log-probability discrepancy
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Calibrating Teacher--Student Discrepancy for On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: Cal-OPD uses contrasting teacher contexts to estimate an interval of likelihood variation and removes the covered part of the original teacher-student gap. Matched-sparsity and scaling controls favor residual calibration in the tested settings, without proving that the removed variation is entirely task-irrelevant.
papers.objective: Residual teacher-student advantages after contextual calibration
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 18 Sep 2026]

papers.title: One to More, More to One: Category-Aware Iterative Expert Training for Software Engineering Agents
papers.description: This software-engineering pipeline trains category experts and consolidates them through teacher feedback on student rollouts. Reported expert-gain retention is 80.8%, 111.1%, and 84.8% across three categories. The Pro-618 evaluation also selects checkpoints; differing training pools and budgets prevent an isolated consolidation advantage.
papers.objective: Executable-outcome reinforcement learning for experts, supervised replay of their verified successes, then label-routed on-policy teacher feedback that retains only improving directions relative to a reference.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Distill What You Trust: Reliability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: TrustMOPD weights specialist teachers at each student-generated prefix using calibrated changes in next-token preferences relative to a shared pre-RL reference. These changes serve as reliability proxies for token-level supervision; the interpretation depends on specialists derived from that common reference.
papers.objective: Minimize token-level, reliability-weighted reverse KL from the student to each teacher on student-generated prefixes; teacher weights are detached during each update.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 20 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 30 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: CLOOPD: Closing the Learner Loop in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: CLOOPD compares additional student actor passes on frozen teacher-scored batches. The reported two-to-three-pass control improves the macro score without extra teacher scoring, while a matched-cap random allocator outperforms the proposed adaptive allocator.
papers.objective: Empirical comparison of repeated student updates using batch-fixed teacher scores and advantages; no claim of an established exact matching gradient.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 21 Sep 2026]

papers.title: 1% of Tokens Can Be Enough: On Gradient Estimation in On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: This study separates useful teacher corrections from the reliability of estimating their gradients from sampled tokens. It approximates a fixed-prefix signal-to-noise measure to select positions in student rollouts, alone or with usefulness scores; sparse supervision still requires generating and scoring complete trajectories in its implementation.
papers.objective: Apply sampled reverse-KL teacher supervision only at selected student-generated token positions; selection uses an approximated gradient signal-to-noise ratio, optionally combined with usefulness scores.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 21 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Train Where the Quantized Model Goes: On-Policy Distillation for Low-Bit Reasoning
papers.description: After fixed-prefix quantization-aware distillation, the student samples through its deployment quantized forward path; a frozen full-precision teacher supervises those student prefixes alongside task-verifier feedback. The stage targets long-form repetition attributed to quantization-amplified exposure bias and starts from a quantization-aware checkpoint.
papers.objective: Dense token-level teacher guidance on quantized student-generated prefixes combined with verifier rewards for mathematical final answers and code-test success.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 22 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Counterfactual Constraint-Conditioned On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Constraint Instruction Following
papers.description: CC-OPD generates student responses under all constraints while a frozen teacher rescores the same tokens with each constraint removed in turn. Summed, clipped likelihood shifts shape the distillation reward; teacher scoring grows with the number of constraints, without requiring additional student rollouts.
papers.objective: Ratio-clipped PPO using a token reward equal to the negative sampled student-minus-teacher log-probability difference plus a weighted, clipped sum of full-context versus leave-one-constraint-out teacher log-likelihood shifts.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 23 Sep 2026]

papers.title: RL Starts before RL: On Policy Distillation for Better Reinforcement Learning
papers.description: This study tests whether distillation on student-generated trajectories prepares a model for later reinforcement learning beyond improving its initial accuracy. In its comparisons, the preferred KL direction changes after RL on student trajectories; that ranking does not extend to teacher-generated trajectories.
papers.objective: Reverse- or forward-KL matching to full teacher token distributions during preparation, followed by separate outcome-verified reinforcement learning.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 23 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 26 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]

papers.title: When and Where to Trust the Teacher: Unifying On-Policy Distillation and GRPO through Entropy-Calibrated Credit Assignment
papers.description: The UECR study separates response-level teacher utility from a mean-preserving redistribution of verifier-derived token credit. A blinded audit at shared initialization compares the resulting weights with labeled reasoning errors and shuffled-entropy controls, without establishing downstream superiority from those diagnostics.
papers.objective: Analyze credit localization under response-wise conservation
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 23 Sep 2026]

papers.title: LastOPD: Taming Collapse in Latent On-Policy Distillation
papers.description: LastOPD aligns the student’s final pre-head representation with the teacher’s on student-generated responses, then fades that latent loss into token-level distillation. The crossfade is motivated by observed collapse under continued latent supervision in the tested cross-size model pairs.
papers.objective: A linearly decreasing final-state alignment loss and increasing reverse top-k student-to-teacher token KL on the same student rollouts; token KL alone after the crossfade.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 23 Sep 2026]

papers.title: Not Every Token Is Worth Distilling: Selective Supervision for Direct-OPD
papers.description: This work shows that a teacher’s post-RL versus pre-RL token log-ratio can remain unchanged as the probability mass behind it vanishes. It ranks student-visited states by teacher–reference divergence and retains log-ratio supervision only at the highest-ranked positions within each response.
papers.objective: At selected student states, apply detached student-top-candidate weights to post-RL/pre-RL teacher log-ratio rewards, together with an initial-student KL penalty. Both terms are masked and averaged over states selected by teacher–reference JSD.
papers.source_version: [Submitted on 24 Sep 2026 ( v1 ), last revised 26 Sep 2026 (this version, v2)]
